notes: 'Proto Loyalties inherited from PNC a simple/geminate distinction in voiceless stops (as well as in nasals)... these geminates in turn became aspirates in PLoy' (p. 164). Lynch also suggests that ungeminated *p was a fricative [β] in PLoy (p. 165); not entered as a change (stated as 'probably').
Labiovelars remain bilabials, losing their labialisation after the labial-to-apical change (p. 163).

*b > d and *m > n when the following vowel was a PLoy front vowel, whether a POc front vowel or *a, *u fronted after a bilabial (p. 164); Lynch (2019a: 301, 305) traces it through a linguolabial stage. The same row from Ozanne-Rivierre (1992) is stated 'before a front vowel'.
As *b (p. 164). Exceptions: *mapo > meu (perhaps a loan from Drehu) and *maqurip > hmor (p. 163, n. 12).
*pʰ > tʰ before front vowels, certainly before *i and probably before *e (p. 164).
Ungeminated *p is lost in all environments, after conditioning vowel changes; Nengone w in *poñu > ce/we (p. 165). Lynch (2019a: 301) gives the same.
PLoy *pʰ > Iaai, Drehu hw before *a ((26), p. 164).
PLoy *pʰ > Iaai, Drehu hw before *a ((26), p. 164).
In Iaai *p is lost before POc *u (which became PLoy *i, Iaai ü) and, in non-initial syllables, before POc *i ((27), p. 164).
Also lost before *o in all three languages ((28)).
Elsewhere retained as non-final β, final p ((29), p. 165).
